clue.text: Right to Left (margin ahead), despicable types are top of the class

indicators.note: reading from the right-hand end towards the left means the assembled string is turned backwards

parts.note: a lip is the edge or rim of something
a team that is ahead is up, as in two goals up
rats are treacherous, contemptible people

explanation.surface: An election-day jibe: politicians lurching from Right to Left are rats, yet claim to be best in the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right to Left' turns the whole string LIPUPRATS backwards; the political sense is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A star pupil is the best-performing student in a class, the one at its top.

clue.text: Dawn for Scottish Nationalists, embracing Union once again?

indicators.note: the union letter is put inside a second time, at a different point in the party initials
the party initials hold the union letter within them

parts.note: SNP is the Scottish National Party
U again, the abbreviation for Union, used for the second insertion
U again, the abbreviation for Union, used for the second insertion

explanation.surface: Would a second union be a new dawn for the Scottish Nationalists, who want to leave the first?
explanation.walkthrough: The U goes into SNP twice, after S and after N, giving S-U-N-U-P.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunup is a chiefly American word for sunrise, the start of the day.

clue.text: A party, eroded Left and Right, is embarrassed

parts.note: a bash is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: the leftmost and rightmost letters of the next word are kept, the rest worn away

explanation.surface: A political party worn down on both its left and right wings feels humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left and Right' sounds like the political wings but picks the outside letters of 'eroded', E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abashed is to feel ashamed or disconcerted, a close synonym.

clue.text: See 26
SDLP are wrongly depicted as hawkers

indicators.note: letters set out wrongly are put in another order

explanation.surface: The Northern Irish SDLP are unfairly portrayed as door-to-door salesmen.
explanation.walkthrough: The SDLP is Northern Ireland's Social Democratic and Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedlars and hawkers are both itinerant sellers of small goods.

clue.text: Quick cut garners approval before rash changes

indicators.note: to garner is to gather in, so the word for cut takes the rest inside it

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

indicators.note: the approval comes ahead of the rearranged letters

parts.note: OK signals approval

indicators.note: the letters of rash undergo changes into a new order

explanation.surface: A quick haircut wins approval before the rash change is regretted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' as the definition is an imperative idiom, not an adjective; 'garners' means the cut takes everything else inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Look sharp is an imperative idiom meaning hurry up, be quick.

clue.text: UKIP notches up gains: a sign of economic failure

indicators.note: letters that are up, as in stirred up, are mixed into another order

explanation.surface: UKIP's electoral gains, the clue suggests, are themselves a symptom of a failing economy.
explanation.walkthrough: UKIP is the UK Independence Party. 'gains' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Queues at charity kitchens serving free food to the needy indicate economic hardship.

clue.text: Old Labour supporter to cause trouble taking on Right

indicators.note: the phrase for causing trouble takes the letter on board, inside it

parts.note: to stir up is to provoke trouble

explanation.surface: An Old Labour stalwart stirs up trouble by taking on the Right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' here is childbirth, not the party: stirrups supported the feet of women in delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetric stirrups were long used to hold a woman's legs during childbirth.

clue.text: Release humanity, first held by moneylender

indicators.note: the pieces are held within the word for a moneylender

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker
man in the sense of mankind
A is first, as in a top grade or the first letter

explanation.surface: Release humanity from debt, first held in the grip of moneylenders.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmanacle someone is to remove their shackles and set them free.

clue.text: Tedious "nu" clue

parts.note: the clue shows the result: the letters U and N, rearranged, give the Greek letter's name

explanation.surface: A clue built on the Greek letter nu is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, the answer tells you to rearrange U and N, producing the 'nu' the clue shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no variety is monotonous and therefore dull.

clue.text: Small bird made of folded paper: one cut and tail twitching

indicators.note: the last two letters flick round, swapping places
the numeral one, as the letter I, is cut from the word

parts.note: origami is the Japanese art of paper folding
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A little paper bird, with a snip and a flick of the tail.
explanation.walkthrough: ORIGAMI loses I to give ORIGAM, then 'tail twitching' swaps its final AM to MA.
explanation.definitionFit: The origma is the rock warbler, a small Australian songbird.

clue.text: Emergency power with feverish result

parts.note: a UPS is an uninterruptible power supply, emergency backup power
a feverish person feels hot

explanation.surface: An emergency power supply leaves things feverish as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the final outcome or consequence of something.

clue.text: Losing candidates present as players wearing sweaters

indicators.note: the players are inside the sweaters, as if wearing them

parts.note: Arans are thick knitted jumpers from the Aran Islands
the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: Defeated candidates show up as performers in woolly jumpers.
explanation.definitionFit: Also-rans are those who compete but finish unplaced, so losers.

clue.text: What's Left? None of Democratic Unionists follow American election primary

indicators.note: the unionist initials come after the other pieces
the primary, or first, letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

explanation.surface: Asking what remains of the Left after unionists follow the American primary season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks political but simply means remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: When nothing is remaining, the supply is exhausted, all consumed.

clue.text: Source of power for free spirit: a deal, I hear?

indicators.note: says the pieces are what is heard, standing for a like-sounding phrase

parts.note: a soul is a spirit freed from the body, then A, then sell, meaning to deal in goods: spoken together they match the two-word answer

explanation.surface: A free spirit seeking power for nothing strikes a deal, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUL-A-SELL, spoken, matches the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A photovoltaic panel unit converts sunlight into electricity, supplying energy.

clue.text: In the pub, Boatman? Drink up and make a connection for talking

parts.note: PH is the abbreviation for public house
the setter refers to himself; one is the impersonal pronoun for oneself

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads backwards

parts.note: to gulp is to drink quickly

explanation.surface: The setter, drinking up in the pub, makes a social connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack on a cord links a telephone to the line so conversation can happen.

clue.text: Imposition of tax covers returning Alliance

indicators.note: the word for covers comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: mats are floor or table coverings
a pact is an agreement or alliance

explanation.surface: A tax rise is concealed in a revived coalition deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stamp Act of 1765 taxed printed paper in the American colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stamp Act was a British statute imposing a duty on colonial documents.

clue.text: Decrepit vehicle for Spooner's emotionless style of music

indicators.note: Spooner switched the starts of words, so the sounds of two words trade places

parts.note: cold means unfeeling
rock is a genre of popular music

explanation.surface: An ancient banger suits a cool, unemotional kind of rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: COLD ROCK, with its opening C shifted, sounds as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An old crock is a worn-out, broken-down car; also a veteran-car rally entrant.

clue.text: Liberal Democrat has no time for fellow socialist

indicators.note: liberal means free, so the letters are freely rearranged
the word goes without the letter for time

explanation.surface: A Lib Dem with no time for socialist allies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal Democrat' reads as the party; 'Liberal' is the anagram sign for DEMOCRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Comrade is the traditional form of address among socialists and communists.

clue.text: See 6 across
Plaid Cymru, oddly muddled about England, sought help

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about, around, the letter for England
the selected letters are muddled into a new order
the odd-numbered letters are taken

explanation.surface: The Welsh nationalists, confused about England, asked for assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd letters of 'Plaid Cymru' give PADYR; 'muddled' makes PRAYD, with E inside. Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist party.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray is to ask, plead, appeal for divine assistance.

clue.text: Broadcast's topical but it fails to connect

parts.note: airs means broadcasts, the 's standing for 'is' giving the verb form
a hot topic is one of current interest

explanation.surface: A topical broadcast that still misses its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: An air shot is a swing in cricket or golf that misses the ball entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: A swing that misses the ball makes no contact with it.

clue.text: Tattoo of devil's head and spirit done in …

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rum is a distilled spirit
beat means exhausted

explanation.surface: A devilish tattoo and a spirit worn out at the end of a long campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tattoo' is not body art but a rhythmic beating.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a rhythmic tapping or drum signal, as in a military tattoo.

clue.text: … support of truly embracing condition

indicators.note: the word for truly holds the condition inside

parts.note: very can mean truly, as in the very truth
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: support for a truthful condition.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify is to confirm, bearing out a claim with evidence.

clue.text: Today you can be awkward — revolt, ejecting head of legislature

indicators.note: awkward letters are put into a different arrangement
the word throws out a letter
the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: On election day you can be awkward and rebel against the legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared on the 2015 UK general election day, so 'Today' points to casting a ballot. REVOT is the remnant of 'revolt'.
explanation.definitionFit: On polling day anyone registered can be one who casts a ballot.

clue.text: Sinn Fein rejects House and forfeits result

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged, the result being a new word
the word for house is thrown out

parts.note: an inn is a public house

explanation.surface: Sinn Fein's refusal to take Commons seats has a cost.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinn Fein MPs do not sit in the House of Commons. SFEIN is left before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Fines are monetary penalties, sums forfeited as punishment.

clue.text: Remove rump of Respect?

parts.note: de- is a prefix meaning remove, as in de-ice
the tail is at the rump of an animal

explanation.surface: Cutting off the rump of the Respect party.
explanation.walkthrough: Respect was a small British left-wing party; here the word means 'particular'.
explanation.definitionFit: In every respect means in every particular point or item.

clue.text: Several fine lines are emerging

definitions.meaning: shading drawn with many close parallel strokes

explanation.surface: Several new lines of policy are appearing.
explanation.definitionFit: In drawing, closely ruled parallel strokes give shading; chicks breaking from eggs emerge.

clue.text: Plan for Conservative and Unionist controlled media at one time …

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservative Party

parts.words: Unionist controlled media at one time
parts.note: the newspaper presses were dominated by trade unions in Fleet Street's heyday

explanation.surface: A scheme for Conservatives and Unionists to control the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unionist' suggests Ulster politics but means trade unionists in the print industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a detailed design or scheme of action.

clue.text: … causes upset in Green seat

indicators.note: an upset throws the letters into another order

explanation.surface: An election shock in a seat taken by the Greens.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to bring about or produce, as a cause does.
